prediction.text:
Nike's revenue fell about 9.8%, from $51.362 billion in fiscal 2024 to $46.309 billion in fiscal 2025, a drop of about $5.05 billion. Nike's 10-K says the currency-neutral decline came mainly from lower revenues in North America, EMEA and Greater China, which cut revenues by 4, 3 and 2 percentage points. Footwear unit sales fell 8%, and a lower average selling price cut footwear revenue by about 3 percentage points. NIKE Direct revenues fell 13%, from $21.5 billion to $18.8 billion. The filing passages retrieved do not give one single cause, such as weak consumer demand.
Nike's revenue was $51.362 billion in fiscal 2024.
Nike's revenue was $46.309 billion in fiscal 2025.
Revenue fell about 9.8% year over year in fiscal 2025, which confirms the decline.
The revenue decline was about $5.05 billion.
Nike's 10-K says revenues decreased 10% reported and 9% currency-neutral. On a currency-neutral basis, it attributed the decrease primarily to lower revenues in North America, EMEA and Greater China, which each reduced NIKE, Inc. Revenues by 4, 3 and 2 percentage points, respectively.
Nike reported that footwear unit sales decreased 8%, and a lower average selling price per pair reduced footwear revenues by approximately 3 percentage points.
By channel, NIKE Direct revenues declined 13%, from $21.5 billion in fiscal 2024 to $18.8 billion in fiscal 2025. Nike said gross margin fell 190 basis points to 42.7%, primarily due to higher discounts, changes in channel mix and higher inventory obsolescence reserves, partly offset by lower product costs.
In North America, the largest regional decline, revenues decreased 8% on a currency-neutral basis. Nike attributed this primarily to lower revenues in the Jordan Brand, Men's and Women's. Wholesale revenues decreased 5%. NIKE Direct revenues decreased 12%, with digital sales down 19% and store sales down 1%.
